I've seen a lot of posts on here about having emergency supplies to survive WWIII, Zombie Apocalypse, and now the Wuhan Flu. It may seem silly to worry about these things as the chance that society will shut down in the near future is almost nil; however, it isn't impossible. So stock up on things just in case.

Buy shelf stable food items that can be used for years. Make sure you have water or purifying supplies (distiller, purifier or chlorine bleach). Have a tent, sleeping bag, and fishing pole. Camping is fun, if you haven't done it go ahead and try it out; buy the gear at a flea market or surplus store. It's always a good idea to have matches, candles, canned food, etc. in case the power goes out.

All the things you would need in a survival situation are just good to have. I live near a huge forest, so I already have a chainsaw, handsaw, axe & hatchet, but if you own your own home these items are useful. Imagine a storm comes by and blows a tree into your driveway on a day that you have an important meeting or job interview. Wouldn't you wish you already had the tools to get your car out of your garage so that you don't miss that meeting? Or if you need to remove a dead tree limb the cost of a chainsaw is not much more than having a tree surgeon come out. My point is, for whatever reason, it's just a good idea to have supplies, tools and food on-hand. And when you're not in a rush you can find a good deal or find used tools and gear at garage sales.

I over prepare because I don't like to rely on other people for things that I am capable of doing myself. Other people aren't reliable, and all of us should be more self sufficient.

Another good tip is to always carry a multi-tool; I can't tell you how many times I've been the only person in a group who had a knife or screwdriver.
